articles.title: This Promising New Soulslike Features A Black Metal Vocalist Among Its Impressive Cast
articles.summary: The main voice actor cast for upcoming soulslike Valor Mortis has been revealed, and its star-studded lineup features the surprising addition of a name better known for fronting a black metal band. Adam "Nergal" Darski will play the role of Captain Raphael.
body: It's not his first rodeo, surprisingly. He also voiced The Black Cat in 2022's Blacktail and was the narrator for Apocalipsis: The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil in 2018.

He's joining an impressive roster of voice actors, including Baldur's Gate 3 and Expedition 33's Jennifer English as The Shrike and Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Crimson Desert's James Alexander as William Dowsett. Napoleon Bonaparte will be played by Vincent Cassel, who has starred in the Ocean's Twelve and Ocean's Thirteen films as François Toulour.

Mars Lipowski, who is best known for portraying Sobieslaw "Gromsko" Kosciuszko in the Call of Duty franchise, will take on the role of Lucjan Skawinski. Will De Renzy-Martin, who played Coen in The Blood of Dawnwalker, will portray James Stewart. Finally, Yvan Chamouiseau will step into the shoes of Louis Moreau.

Valor Mortis is a first-person action soulslike from the developer of Ghostrunner. Set in an alternate 19th century Eastern Europe, Napoleon's endless war has led to a supernatural plague. You'll follow William, played by Alexander, as he fights to survive against his former comrades who are now undead monsters.
points: The main voice actor cast for upcoming soulslike Valor Mortis has been revealed, and its star-studded lineup features the surprising addition of a name better known for fronting a black metal band.
Adam "Nergal" Darski will play the role of Captain Raphael.
He also voiced The Black Cat in 2022's Blacktail and was the narrator for Apocalipsis: The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil in 2018.

articles.title: Witcher Fans Are Eating Well
articles.summary: If you're a fan of The Witcher franchise, you're getting a lot of new stuff over the next few years, starting this week with the launch of The Witcher 3 Remastered. Here's what's on tap for The Witcher over the next few years: 2026.
body: The Witcher 3 Remastered, which includes a bevy of technical and graphical updates and improvements, releases on September 29. The long-awaited remaster, which is free for people who already own the game, includes a reimagined skill system, an expanded photo mode, improved combat, and a new transmog feature. Check out GameSpot's in-depth breakdown of what's new in the remaster to find out more. Just be aware, the graphical overhaul isn't necessarily an entirely positive one.

After that will come a new expansion for The Witcher 3, Songs of the Past, in 2027. The expansion was originally targeting a 2026 release, but it was pushed to 2027 to make it as good and polished as possible.

Songs of the Past takes Geralt on one last ride “before passing the torch.” Players will venture to the location of Letten, home of Geralt's friendly bard companion, Dandelion. There is a new main quest called "A Bed of Thorns" where Geralt will meet up with Lilla, who appears to be a potential love interest for Geralt.
Also in 2027? That's when The Witcher author Andrzej Sapkowski said he plans to finish the next entry in the novel series, telling the next Geralt of Rivia story.

articles.title: Behold, The $60 Gears Of War Pizza Cutter That Looks Like A Real Pain In The Butt To Clean
articles.summary: Xbox has announced its next collaboration, and it's a partnership with Prince St. Pizza for a specially branded Gears of War pizza and a $60 pizza-cutter. Microsoft and Prince St.
body: Microsoft and Prince St. Pizza teamed up to make a Prototype Lancer pizza-cutter to promote this October's Gears of War: E-Day, and it's available for $60. To justify the steep price tag, Prince St. Pizza says it's a hefty metal cutter featuring a stainless steel blade and a handle that's meant to make you feel like you're wielding the iconic gun. The pizza-cutter also comes with the in-game pizza emblem. It does look pretty great, but it also looks like a real pain the butt to clean if you're a messy person like me.

If anyone is wondering why it's called the Prototype Lancer and not just the Lancer, that's the special solution the developers came up with to explain why the heck a Lancer would even be in a prequel like E-Day. In the Gears of War lore, the weapon was created a year after the events of Emergence Day. However, you can't have a Gears game without the Lancer, so the developers called it a Prototype Lancer.

articles.title: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life Drops Below $200
articles.summary: One of the best wireless gaming headsets just dropped to its lowest price ever. Woot, which is owned by Amazon, is offering a new Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for PS5, PS4, and PC for just $191.99 after you apply 20% off coupon code " CHEERS ".
body: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro has long been one of IGN's highest rated wireless gaming headsets. IGN's Kevin Lee gave the Nova Pro a 10/10 "Masterpiece" review and I believe it still holds today. I've clocked well over a thousand hours on mine to the point that my earcups were worn through (I replaced them with the awesome WC Freeze gel earpads ). SteelSeries released a successor - the Nova Pro Omni - earlier this year, but it currently sells for $380 and the improvements are certainly not worth the nearly $200 price premium. The Omni's pièce de résistance is its seamless cross-platform switching. If you predominantly use these headphones for one platform, then stick with the Nova Pros.

The one feature that undoubtedly makes the Nova Pro stand out amongst the crowd is the ingenious hot-swappable battery system. The Nova Pro includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your headset and the other to remain charged and ready to go in a base station that doubles as a charger. This way, you get wireless freedom with zero downtime. Each battery lasts for up to 22 hours of continued use so you don't need to swap out too often.
points: One of the best wireless gaming headsets just dropped to its lowest price ever.

articles.title: The Last of Us Day Reveals Ghost of Yotei Collab Content and Ambience Video as Fans Beg Naughty Dog for TLOU 3
articles.summary: Naughty Dog has revealed that it's celebrating The Last of Us Day 2026 with Ghost of Yotei content, player avatars on PlayStation and Steam, and an hour-long ambience video as fans continue begging for any updates on The Last of Us Part 3.
body: It's… probably not what you or anyone else was expecting to see when the Sony studio teased plans for its annual holiday over the weekend. Instead of confirmation for The Last of Us Part 3 (or even yet, another remaster of an existing title), Naughty Dog instead revealed a collection of smaller surprises to keep fans tied over.

The headline is no doubt an armor set that's coming to Sucker Punch Productions' Ghost of Yotei. Available starting October 1, players will be able to hop into the sequel's Most Wanted mode while sporting Clicker-inspired armor. After it's unlocked, players will be able to use it in the base game, as well as its new Echoes of Sekigahara DLC. You can see a first look at The Last of Us armor below.

So, what else is there for The Last of Us Day 2026? Naughty Dog also announced a partnership with collectible company Youtooz for a Bloody Clicker figure. In addition to the previously revealed Welcome Hub background wallpaper for PS5, PlayStation users can enjoy four new themed avatars, with even more available on PC via Steam.

The highest-grossing Resident Evil movie globally is Resident Evil: The Final Chapter, which made $312 million worldwide. Time will tell if 2026's Resident Evil will catch up.

articles.title: Forget 'Delicious in Dungeon,' This Cozy Fantasy Graphic Novel Hits the Same Notes
articles.summary: Progression fantasy books like Will Wight’s Cradle series or Matt Dinniman’s Dungeon Crawler Carl usually draw on role-playing game tropes to focus on characters gaining new powers they use to face more dangerous foes.
body: It’s easy to want to step into the fantasy world of Thune, where Viv finds new friends like the shy ratkin baker Thimble and taciturn carpenter Cal as she turns an old stable into a cozy café. You can get closer with Legends & Lattes: The Graphic Novel, adapted by Samuel Sattin and illustrated by Shanti Rittgers and Sarah Webb.

“This is the first time I've had something like this done on this scale for my own book,” Baldree tells Polygon via email. "I was really happy with how true to the original book the adaptation turned out and astonished at the sheer amount of work to produce a graphic novel of this length.”

The graphic novel will be released in hardcover, e-book, and a signed deluxe edition with colored page edges on Oct. 6. Ahead of its release, publisher Ten Speed Graphic gave Polygon an exclusive excerpt that shows Viv sharing coffee with Cal and recruiting an assistant, the succubus Tandri.
“I think Viv's introduction of coffee to Cal really comes across as an ASMR-like experience – it's lovely!" Baldree says.

articles.title: Where to find yuna mei in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: In Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, you will need yuna mei to rebuild one of the destroyed temples once you reach Part 3. Completing the side quests during the last arc in the game is the best way to prepare your units for the final battle, as you level up and collect powerful rewards.
body: Since this is a rather rare material, we can help by explaining where to find yuna mei in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

If you want some yuna mei, there are two places for you to visit. The first is the Traveler's Garden in Castalia, on the northeast side of the map. This is the best node to collect yuna mei because of how close it is to the Eochaid Posthouse, which you can travel to by carriage.

The other node where you can find yuna mei is Cape Damaise, also in Castalia. To reach the place, head west of Fina, on the north coast. Although you can travel to the Eochaid Posthouse and go to Cape Damaise, you will spend more turns than you would if you chose to visit the Traveler's Garden instead, making it the least optimal farming spot.

Regardless of the node you choose, yuna mei is the rarest material in both of them. Collecting one will require a few tries, so consider saving before using the "Search" command to quickly load the game if you don't find any after a few tries. Another option is to leave a battalion if you're either playing Theodora's path or taking a group that has Theodora as a member to the node.
points: In Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, you will need yuna mei to rebuild one of the destroyed temples once you reach Part 3.
Completing the side quests during the last arc in the game is the best way to prepare your units for the final battle, as you level up and collect powerful rewards.

articles.title: "What if London existed in the Grand Theft Auto universe?" One fan has answered with a GTA-style map of the city
articles.summary: What if Rockstar created a GTA game set in London?" Anyone sitting in the venn diagram centre of GTA fan and cartography sicko might be happy to learn that YouTuber CityEd has answered both of those questions with a GTA-style map.
body: "I've created a GTA-ised map of London imagining how the map would look, and re-invented place names in a classic GTA style," CityEd wrote on their Patreon, where you can also find a PDF copy of their map. "For instance, Kings Cross becomes 'Dukes Cross', Angel becomes 'Saint'', and the whole city becomes 'Trafalgar'."

CityEd's thought experiment aimed to carry Rockstar Games ' naming conventions across the pond - that includes the developer's signature satire, "exaggerated landmarks and GTA-style cartography" - using the studio's past games as a reference point.

"While the cities and places they base their maps on exist in real life, they have this fun convention for creating fictional place names where they find something historically or culturally associated with the place, exaggerate it, and use that instead," they explained.

As they also noted, Rockstar's last trip to the English capital wasn't much help at all. 1999's GTA: London mission pack came out before the studio began reimagining city names in fun ways, so CityEd's version had to start from scratch.
points: What if Rockstar created a GTA game set in London?

articles.title: Blizzard's MOBA Is Making An Unexpected Comeback
articles.summary: At BlizzCon 2026, Blizzard Entertainment announced a new hero for Heroes of the Storm: Xal’atath. She's now available in Blizzard's MOBA, after a stint on the game's public test realm, and could signal a larger return of support for the game.
body: World of Warcraft players will recognize Xal’atath as the Harbinger of the Void and a major player in the MMO’s recent Midnight expansion.

Xal’atath is the first new Heroes of the Storm character in nearly six years. The most recent release was Hogger in December 2020, a year after Blizzard ended active development on HotS. Blizzard indicated at BlizzCon that Xal’atath may not be a one-off; depending on player response, the company said it may consider adding additional heroes to the game.

Heroes of the Storm was initially released in 2015 and was Blizzard’s answer to the multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) craze. The game featured heroes from across Blizzard's brands, with playable characters borrowed from Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, and Overwatch. While the genre had emerged in the custom game and modding communities of Warcraft 3, Blizzard’s official MOBA lagged behind games like League of Legends and Dota 2, never finding the same level of success as those titles.

articles.title: Control Resonant Proves Everything Is a Live-Service Game Now
articles.summary: A few weeks before its official Sept. 24 launch date, I played through Control Resonant — in some form. The version of Remedy Entertainment’s trippy action RPG you can play today is so different from what I played that it may as well be entirely new to me.
body: It also reveals the slippery nature of modern games. In an age where developers can completely overhaul a game on the fly, it becomes more challenging to know when the best time to play a game is. Do you jump in on day one to satiate your hype, or do you give it a few weeks, a month, or even year once patches iron out the frustrations that the early birds dealt with? In today’s gaming landscape, patience is increasingly a virtue.

If you’re playing Control Resonant today and scratching your head about early reviews that criticized its combat, here’s what the game was like pre-patch. Previously, enemies were pure damage sponges. While the puny Hiss critters were easy to take out, anything bigger than that required a lot of slashing to take down. The relief was supposed to come from Resonant ’s Falter status effect, a stagger system that allows Dylan to zip directly to enemies and execute them. But the amount of times you’d need to hit an enemy to fill their Falter gauge was so high that you were more likely to just kill them the old-fashioned way first.

articles.title: Ubisoft's calling its next push into gen-AI game development Motherbrain
articles.summary: Ubisoft is internally calling its latest generative-AI initiative 'Motherbrain' - you know, like the evil supercomputer turned gross brain-in-a-jar monster from Nintendo's Metroid series - according to trademarks filed by the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publisher.
body: As first reported on by The Game File and spotted by Kotaku, a bunch of recent trademark applications use the definitely-not-ominous Motherbrain term to refer to the company's various gen-AI plans.

According to the report, one trademark makes mention of a "downloadable computer software using artificial intelligence (AI) for creating video games and interactive content." Another refers to an AI service used for both "analyzing data and interacting with humans," and the research and design of "software using artificial intelligence."

Ubisoft hasn't mentioned Motherbrain to the public just yet. The term is seemingly only being used inside of the publisher's walls, but Ubisoft's been pretty openly enthusiastic about the controversial tech and its possible applications in game development for a while.

articles.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered is an extraordinarily generous upgrade that doesn't change the game, but does make it new again
articles.summary: It's tricky to appraise the Remastered edition of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt because on the one hand, everything about it is extraordinary. It's a free upgrade to an 11-year-old game that showcases a level of support and generosity I don't think I've seen for any other single-player game, ever.
body: However, it does also feel a bit purposeless without a Songs of the Past expansion to play with it - assuming you weren't already considering a replay of the game, or going back to finish the main campaign (which you need to have finished for Songs of the Past), or playing the expansions. All good reasons to go back. What I'm saying is that alone, if you've already played it before, the Remastered edition won't necessarily keep you entertained for longer than a few hours while you tour the game to see what's new.

To put it more bluntly, the Remastered edition doesn't fundamentally change The Witcher 3. If you were somehow hoping this remaster overhauls the game's combat, for example, I'm sorry to tell you that it doesn't. Indeed, it can be quite challenging to work out what is actually new when you're playing it. Most of the time, it's The Witcher 3 game we all remember, however long the list of changes is - though perhaps it's more accurate to say it's The Witcher 3 that lives in our memory.
points: It's tricky to appraise the Remastered edition of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt because on the one hand, everything about it is extraordinary.

videos.title: Minecraft Dungeons 2 Review
videos.summary: Minecraft Dungeons 2 reviewed by Travis Northup on Xbox Series X, also available on PC, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch.
body: "Minecraft Dungeons 2 is a shallow ARPG that offers a few evenings of mindless dungeon delving fun, but not much beyond that. Aside from the new Sift realm, which has some cool new ideas and creatures to admire as you and your friends carve your way through it, there’s just not much to make this sequel stand out. It makes poor use of Minecraft’s iconic world, feeling like little more than a skin slapped onto a generic Diablo-like, with a barebones story and skin-deep hack-and-slash combat. This low-stakes action isn’t a bad way to pass the time, especially if you’re intimidated by the hilariously crunchy menus and buildcrafting of more serious ARPGs, but there also aren’t a ton of compelling reasons to play this one beyond that."

videos.title: Kalanoro – Launch Trailer – Nintendo Switch
videos.summary: Play Kalanoro now on Nintendo Switch:
body: Hop on a colorful action-adventure inspired by Malagasy folklore! Recruit legendary lemur musicians, grow your band's fame across Lemuria, and challenge the evil witch Raneny in a quest to save the island—one song at a time!

Once a paradise, the island of Lemuria now suffers under Raneny’s ruthless rule. Having grown tired of exploiting its people, she decided to host a huge concert with the island’s most famous band. You’re sent on a mission to fight back by rallying legendary musicians to your cause!

Dash through diverse biomes, save and befriend funky locals to form your crew, and jump over industrial platforming traps to become Lemuria’s number one band and finally face Raneny. Defeat her minions in fast-paced combat, using hair-based powers and improvised weapons (slippers included). Fight epic and groovy boss battles, and free the island!
